sections.title: Overview
sections.content: The Energy Analysis Skill provides diagnostic analysis of facility energy consumption data: pattern identification, anomaly detection, opportunity identification, and carbon footprint calculation. It works only on facility-level data for facilities in the built-in database (facility_id format FAC + 3 digits); do not trigger it for vehicle emissions, product footprints, energy-market or policy questions, or anything without a facility context.

sections.title: When to Use
sections.content: Use this skill when the user: Describes concerns about a specific facility's energy consumption or costs; Asks to analyze a facility's usage patterns or find anomalies; Wants to calculate a facility's carbon emissions; Mentions a facility's high bills or unusual consumption. Do NOT use this skill when: The request concerns non-facility emissions (vehicles, products, supply chains); The request is about energy markets, policy, or ESG reporting; No facility is identified and the user cannot provide a facility_id; The user asks for concrete implementation recommendations or per-measure savings estimates - use the efficiency_optimization skill instead (this skill reports only the diagnostic estimated_savings_potential percentage)

sections.title: Input Handling
sections.content: Required inputs: facility_id (format FAC + 3 digits, e.g., FAC001) always; plus analysis period (start_date, end_date, YYYY-MM-DD) only for energy_analyze_consumption and energy_calculate_carbon_footprint. facility_id comes from the user; never fabricate it. When input is incomplete or ambiguous, ask the user instead of guessing. max_items applies to user-submitted request items: process at most 10 per interaction. One facility per interaction; the tools accept a single facility_id per call. If the user submits multiple facilities, ask them to pick one first.

sections.title: Available Operations
sections.content: 1. energy_analyze_consumption - Analyze energy consumption data to identify patterns and anomalies. Parameters: facility_id (required, FAC + 3 digits), start_date (required, YYYY-MM-DD), end_date (required, YYYY-MM-DD), granularity (optional: hourly/daily/monthly, default daily). Returns (closed enumeration): total_consumption, peak_demand, average_daily, patterns, anomalies, benchmark_comparison. Usage notes: requires at least 7 days of data for meaningful pattern analysis; anomaly detection uses statistical deviation from rolling averages; benchmarks based on facility type and region. 2. energy_identify_efficiency_opportunities - Identify energy efficiency improvement opportunities based on consumption analysis. Parameters: facility_id (required), analysis_results (optional, prior results from energy_analyze_consumption). Returns (closed enumeration): opportunities (each with only opportunity_type, description, estimated_savings_potential, confidence), priority_order. Usage notes: best used after energy_analyze_consumption for context; identifies and diagnoses opportunities, does not produce implementation recommendations (efficiency_optimization skill). 3. energy_calculate_carbon_footprint - Calculate carbon footprint from energy consumption data. Parameters: facility_id (required), start_date (required), end_date (required), include_breakdown (optional, default true). Returns (closed enumeration): total_emissions_kgco2, emission_intensity, breakdown (electricity, natural gas), comparison. Usage notes: region-specific emission factors for electricity; natural gas uses standard EPA emission factors; Scope 2 reporting method (market-based vs location-based) is not a tool parameter; present both interpretations when relevant.

sections.title: Execution Limits
sections.content: Maximum retries per tool call: 3. Timeout: 60 seconds per call. Maximum tool calls per execution: 10. Limit each response to at most 1,000 English words. Partial results are acceptable. When information is insufficient for a section, skip it or mark it as 'information not available'.

sections.title: Failure Handling Policy
sections.content: If a tool call fails, report the error to the user. You may retry the identical call at most 3 times (per max_retries); if the retry also fails, stop immediately, report the error, and do not attempt alternative tools or workarounds. After a failure, do not expand the task scope, fabricate data to fill gaps (e.g., invented anomalies, benchmarks, or emission figures), or lower quality standards. The max_items: 10 declaration applies to user-submitted request items only. Tool RESULT payloads may contain up to 50 anomalies or 24 peak-hour entries per the tool schema; when validating findings, review the tool result's data object but limit the presented summary to at most 10 findings.

sections.title: Permissions and Environment Boundaries
sections.content: Allowed operations: read, list, and query. Prohibited: write, update, delete, insert, and overwrite. Use only the declared local data files (data/consumption_patterns.json, data/facilities.json, data/equipment.json). Do not access conversation history, external systems, production databases, production APIs, live systems, or unauthorized external services. Chained invocation: this skill may invoke only the three tools under allowed_operations. Invoking other skills or tools is prohibited.

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.content: Consumption data, facility information, and emission factors come from: data/consumption_patterns.json - Sample consumption records; data/facilities.json - Facility configurations; data/equipment.json - Equipment inventories.

sections.title: Important Constraints
sections.content: Carbon calculations use illustrative emission factors; production use should integrate verified regional data. All findings should be validated against actual operational data before making decisions (bounded by the 10-finding limit above).

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: The Efficiency Optimization Skill generates actionable recommendations for reducing facility energy consumption and costs, and estimates savings from specific efficiency measures. This skill focuses on the 'what to do' phase - transforming analysis insights into concrete action items with cost-benefit analysis.

sections.title: When to Use
sections.content: Use this skill when the user: Asks for facility-specific energy-saving recommendations; Wants to estimate savings from proposed efficiency measures; Mentions facility energy efficiency goals or facility energy cost reduction targets. Do NOT use this skill when: The request concerns non-energy cost reduction (labor, materials, logistics); The request concerns general efficiency questions without a facility context; The user asks about equipment procurement, engineering design, or executing/implementing measures; The user asks for consumption analysis or carbon calculations - use the energy_analysis skill instead.

sections.title: Trigger Precondition
sections.content: Fire this skill's operations exactly when the system prompt's Conversation Flow Step 4 reaches them: facility_id confirmed by the user (Required Inputs gathered). This skill adds no extra condition - the system prompt's workflow is the single source of the trigger rule.

sections.title: Input Handling
sections.content: facility_id comes from the user (format FAC + 3 digits); never fabricate it. The measures list for energy_estimate_savings comes from measures the user requests. When input is incomplete or ambiguous, ask the user instead of guessing. Never invent measure types or efficiency values. The measures array is capped at 10 items per call by the tool. If the user requests more than 10 measures, ask which 10 are most important first.

sections.title: Available Operations
sections.content: 1. energy_recommend_optimizations - Generate specific efficiency recommendations for a facility. Parameters: facility_id (required, FAC + 3 digits), focus_areas (optional, 1-4 strings from: hvac/lighting/equipment/operations), budget_constraint (optional, 0-10,000,000), target_savings (optional, 0-100). Returns (closed enumeration): recommendations (each with only recommendation_id, category, description, estimated_annual_savings_kwh, estimated_annual_cost_savings, implementation_cost, payback_period_months, priority), total_potential_savings, implementation_sequence. Usage notes: recommendations based on facility type and consumption patterns; cost estimates are approximate; all recommendations require engineering validation before implementation. 2. energy_estimate_savings - Calculate projected savings from specific efficiency measures. Parameters: facility_id (required), measures (required, 1-10 measures each with only measure_type: hvac/lighting/equipment/process/envelope; scope optional as percentage string e.g. '50%', default '100%'; efficiency_improvement 0-100). Returns (closed enumeration): measure_analyses (baseline_consumption, projected_consumption, annual_savings_kwh, annual_cost_savings, confidence_interval), total_savings, assumptions. Usage notes: requires baseline consumption data for the facility, else the tool reports an error; confidence intervals reflect uncertainty in efficiency gains; actual savings may vary based on operational conditions.

sections.title: Execution Limits
sections.content: Maximum retries per tool call: 3. Timeout: 60 seconds per call. Maximum tool calls per execution: 10. Limit each response to at most 1,000 English words. Partial results are acceptable. When information is insufficient for a section, skip it or mark it as 'information not available'.

sections.title: Failure Handling Policy
sections.content: If a tool call fails (e.g., energy_estimate_savings reports missing baseline data), stop immediately, report the error, and tell the user what is missing. Do not attempt alternatives. After a failure, do not expand the task scope, fabricate data to fill gaps (e.g., invented baseline consumption or savings figures), or lower quality standards.

sections.title: Does Not Do (non_goals)
sections.content: Does not perform consumption analysis or carbon calculations (use the energy_analysis skill). Does not implement or execute any measure. Does not provide engineering approval. Does not infer from conversation history or add facts that were not provided.

sections.title: Permissions and Environment Boundaries
sections.content: Allowed operations: read, list, and query. Prohibited: write, update, delete, insert, and overwrite. Use only the declared local data files. Do not access conversation history, external systems, production databases, production APIs, live systems, or unauthorized external services. Chained invocation: this skill may invoke only the two tools under allowed_operations. Invoking other skills or tools is prohibited.

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.content: Efficiency measures and their typical impacts come from: data/efficiency_measures.json - Measure library with typical savings ranges; data/equipment.json - Equipment efficiency benchmarks; data/consumption_patterns.json - Baseline consumption data.

sections.title: Important Constraints
sections.content: All cost estimates are approximate and should be validated with actual contractor quotes. Recommendations do not constitute engineering approval. Savings projections are based on typical outcomes; actual results depend on implementation quality and operational conditions. Always include the safety disclaimer: '⚠️ This recommendation requires review and approval by qualified engineering staff before implementation.'

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: The Renewable Integration Skill provides planning-level guidance on adopting renewable energy sources for facility operations. It covers solar PV, wind energy, and energy storage through the single authorized tool energy_suggest_renewables, helping users understand potential, indicative sizing, and simple payback. It works only for facilities in the built-in database; do not trigger it for ESG reporting, carbon accounting, residential solar, maintenance of existing installations, or grid interconnection applications.

sections.title: When to Use
sections.content: Use this skill when the user: Asks about solar panel or wind turbine feasibility for a specific facility; Wants to assess renewable energy potential for a facility in the database; Explicitly mentions solar, wind, storage, or renewables for a facility (the system prompt's Conversation Flow Step 5 trigger sentence is the single trigger rule; do NOT activate for bare ESG/sustainability/carbon-accounting mentions without an explicit solar/wind/storage/renewables question). Do NOT use this skill when: The request concerns ESG/sustainability reporting or carbon accounting; The request concerns residential solar or non-facility installations; The request concerns maintenance of existing installations or grid interconnection applications; No facility is identified and the user cannot provide a facility_id.

sections.title: Input Handling
sections.content: facility_id comes from the user (format FAC + 3 digits, e.g., FAC001); never fabricate it. When input is incomplete or ambiguous, ask the user instead of guessing. renewable_types accepts at most 3 values from 'solar', 'wind', 'storage'; if the user requests more types or unspecified options, ask them to choose. One facility per interaction; the tool accepts a single facility_id per call. If the user submits multiple facilities, ask them to pick one first.

sections.title: Available Operations
sections.content: 1. energy_suggest_renewables - Provide renewable energy integration recommendations including suitability assessment, indicative sizing, and simple payback estimates. Parameters: facility_id (required, FAC + 3 digits), renewable_types (optional, 1-3 values from solar/wind/storage, default ['solar']), target_coverage (optional, 0-100, default 50). Returns (closed enumeration): Renewable options with suitability assessment, indicative capacity, estimated annual generation, and simple payback estimates; Constraints and caveats for each option. Usage notes: all outputs are planning-level estimates, not engineering designs; sizing and payback outputs are indicative and do not constitute investment advice; actual installations require professional site assessment, utility approval, and permits; financial returns beyond simple payback (NPV, IRR, financing analysis) are out of scope.

sections.title: Execution Limits
sections.content: Maximum retries per tool call: 3. Timeout: 60 seconds per call. Maximum tool calls per execution: 10. Limit each response to at most 1,000 English words. Partial results are acceptable: if only some requested renewable types can be assessed or site data is incomplete, present what was assessed and mark the rest as 'information not available'.

sections.title: Failure Handling Policy
sections.content: If a tool call fails (invalid facility_id, missing site data), stop immediately and report the error. Do not attempt alternatives. After a failure, do not expand the task scope, fabricate data to fill gaps (e.g., invented irradiance, cost, or payback figures), or lower quality standards.

sections.title: Does Not Do (non_goals)
sections.content: Does not provide engineering designs, NPV/IRR/financing analysis, or investment advice. Does not perform efficiency audits or consumption analysis (use the other skills). Does not infer from conversation history or add facts that were not provided.

sections.title: Permissions and Environment Boundaries
sections.content: Allowed operations: read, list, and query. Prohibited: write, update, delete, insert, and overwrite. Use only the declared local data files (data/renewable_options.json, data/facilities.json). Do not access conversation history, external systems, production databases, production APIs, live systems, or unauthorized external services. Chained invocation: this skill may invoke only energy_suggest_renewables. Invoking other skills or tools is prohibited.

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.content: Renewable energy data comes from: data/renewable_options.json - Equipment specifications and costs; data/facilities.json - Site characteristics.

sections.title: Important Constraints
sections.content: Renewable potential estimates are simplified; professional site assessments are required for actual installations. Grid connection requirements vary significantly by utility. All recommendations should be validated with licensed installers and local authorities. Include disclaimer: '⚠️ Renewable energy installations require professional engineering assessment, utility approval, and applicable permits. These estimates are for planning purposes only.'

content.name: energy_analyze_consumption
content.description: Analyze energy consumption patterns and detect anomalies. Analyzes consumption data for a facility over a specified period, identifying usage patterns, peak demand, and anomalies. Returns structured analysis results.

facility_id.description: Facility identifier from the facility database (format: FAC followed by 3 digits, e.g., FAC001).

content.name: energy_calculate_carbon_footprint
content.description: Calculate carbon footprint from energy consumption. Calculates carbon emissions from electricity and natural gas consumption using region-specific emission factors. Returns total emissions and breakdown by energy source.

facility_id.description: Facility identifier from the facility database (format: FAC followed by 3 digits, e.g., FAC001).

include_breakdown.description: Include breakdown by energy source. Default: true.

content.name: energy_estimate_savings
content.description: Estimate savings from specific efficiency measures. Calculates projected energy and cost savings from proposed efficiency measures using baseline consumption data and expected efficiency improvements.

facility_id.description: Facility identifier from the facility database (format: FAC followed by 3 digits, e.g., FAC001). Baseline consumption is inferred from this facility's recorded data.

measures.description: List of efficiency measures to evaluate (1-10 items).

scope.description: Percentage of facility affected, formatted as a percentage string (e.g., '50%'). Default: '100%'.

content.name: energy_identify_efficiency_opportunities
content.description: Identify energy efficiency improvement opportunities. Analyzes facility data and consumption patterns to identify potential areas for energy efficiency improvements. Returns categorized opportunities with estimated savings potential.

analysis_results.description: Optional prior results object returned by a previous energy_analyze_consumption call. If omitted, recent data is analyzed instead. Do not pass user-supplied free-form data.

facility_type_average.description: Average daily kWh for the facility type.

peak_hours.description: Hours of day with peak load (0-23).

items.description: Hour of day with peak load, 0-23.

weekday_weekend_ratio.description: Ratio of weekday to weekend consumption.

total_consumption_kwh.description: Total kWh consumed during the period.

facility_id.description: Facility identifier from the facility database (format: FAC followed by 3 digits, e.g., FAC001).

content.name: energy_recommend_optimizations
content.description: Generate specific energy efficiency recommendations. Provides actionable recommendations with cost-benefit analysis, including estimated savings, implementation costs, and payback periods. Recommendations are tailored to facility type and available opportunities.

budget_constraint.description: Optional maximum implementation budget in local currency. Recommendations exceeding this budget are excluded.

facility_id.description: Facility identifier from the facility database (format: FAC followed by 3 digits, e.g., FAC001).

focus_areas.description: Optional list of areas to focus recommendations on. Allowed values: hvac, lighting, equipment, operations.

items.description: One focus area: hvac, lighting, equipment, or operations.

target_savings.description: Optional target savings percentage (0-100) to guide recommendations.

content.name: energy_suggest_renewables
content.description: Provide renewable energy integration recommendations. Analyzes facility characteristics and location to provide recommendations for solar, wind, and other renewable energy options. Includes suitability assessment, sizing guidance, and ROI projections.

facility_id.description: Facility identifier from the facility database (format: FAC followed by 3 digits, e.g., FAC001). Facility location and characteristics are looked up from this ID.

renewable_types.description: Types of renewables to assess. Default: ['solar'].

items.description: One renewable type: solar, wind, or storage.

target_coverage.description: Target percentage of consumption to cover (0-100). Default: 50.
